content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a lightweight SISR model (SCNet) with fully 1×1 convolutions. To aggregate local features along the channel dimension, the authors extend the 1×1 convolution into the shift-conv with the spatial-shift operation. Such design of the 1×1 convolution has fewer parameters and less computational cost than the 3x3 convolution. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SCNet.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. This paper proposes a new lightweight SISR model (SCNet) with only 1×1 convolutions.
2. The design of the spatial-shift operation has no extra computational cost and involves local feature aggregation.

Weaknesses:
1. Some technical details are not clear. Please refer to detailed comments in the next section.
2. The advantage of the 1x1 convolution over the transformer-based method should be highlighted.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The advantage of the 1x1 convolution over the transformer-based SR method is not clear. The MLP layers can be regarded as 1x1 convolutions and they are often used in the transformer-based SR method. However, the 1x1 convolution seems to be worse than the transformer-based SR method, e.g., lightweight SwinIR.

2. The 1x1 convolution has limitations to exploit non-local information. Such non-local information is important in many datasets. Can you provide some discussions about it?

3. Some details of Figure 1 are not clear. Which one is an input image or kernel? Which are the projected feature maps and final projected feature maps? Besides, it would be better to use mathematical formulation to prove the equivalence.

4. In Figures 2 and 5, it would be better to compare with lightweight SwinIR.

5. In Table 1, lightweight SwinIR with fewer parameters performs better than SCNet-L. Taking an example on Urban100, The PSRN of lightweight SwinIR is 26.47db which is better than SCNet-L of 26.44db. It would be better to provide more discussions.
content.summary_of_the_review: Some technical details, the advantage of the 1x1 convolution and comparisons are important and should be provided in the paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to use only $1\times1$ convolution with the spatial-shift operation for super-resolution. This design largely reduces the number of parameters while keeping the model capacity. Experiments show that the proposed method can achieve slightly better performance with fewer parameters than other methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
1. The proposed method enlarges the receptive field of $1\times1$ convolution with a spatial-shift operation, which increases the model capacity while keeping the model size and computational cost.

2. My main concern is about the performance. According to Table 1, compared with ShuffleMixer,  the proposed SCNet can only achieve slightly better performance but with 41.2\% more parameters. Moreover, the spatial-shift operation seems to be time-consuming. The authors are suggested to add comparisons on the inference speed.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The idea is interesting and clearly illustrated. The details seem to be sufficient to re-implement these experiments.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed idea is interesting while may have little superiority against previous methods.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
1 × 1 CONVOLUTION IS ALL YOU NEED FOR
LIGHTWEIGHT IMAGE SUPER-RESOLUTION

In the article, the authors propose a neural network architecture based solely on 1 x 1 convolutions. While the proposed operation is faster, it has the potential to reduce the quality of the extracted features. To address that issue, the authors proposed a shift-conv layer, which shifts the features in several directions to obtain representations of some of the missed spatial directions. The authors provide results where their paradigm is tested with five datasets and compared with other lightweight architectures.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths include the development of a fully 1 x 1 convolution neural network, addressing the aggregation of spatial features. I like the employment of several datasets and the study of alternative architectures. I also like the ablation studies that drive some of the design decisions.
I feel that the results are competitive with the alternatives. Yes, they use a reduced number of parameters. However, the hardware restrictions they are addressing are unclear, and whether the number of parameters reduction really makes a difference in the models available for particular computer architecture.

I would like a deeper analysis of the implications of employing 1 x 1 convolution regarding other filter sizes. Although the argument makes intuitive sense, the paper follows the trend where in Deep Learning, we seem to explore by trial and error and not by deep analysis of the consequences of the design choices. 

The source code does not seem available.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The manuscript requires another review of the usage of English, but it is understandable.
They include an algorithm with Pytorch-style pseudocode. However, I did not find a link to the source code.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is easy to read, although some edition to the document needs to be done. The idea is incrementally new, but the performance is not definitive. The architecture brings reminiscences from inception but includes the shift-conv layer to deal with spatial aggregation. The performance is competitive but often not the best. The ablation study is compelling and addresses issues related to previous design choices.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a shift-conv operation to achieve better trade-off between accuracy and efficiency for image super-resolution. Specifically, to leverage the efficiency advantage of 1x1 convolution and to overcome the intrinsic drawback of its context modelling ability, the channels of input features are first spatially shifted with specific design, then 1x1 convolution is performed, such that the receptive field of the layer is effectively enlarged. Comparable or superior performances are demonstrated in five benchmark SR datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

1. Clear writing style and self-contained presentation.

Weaknesses:
1. Limited novelty and missing important relevant work. My first concern is the unprofessional literature comparison. The shift-conv operation is originally proposed in [1], and its temporal version is then proposed in [2]. However, neither comparison nor citation are found in the manuscript. The authors should elaborate the technical difference between [1].
2. Less satisfactory results. The reported results are only comparable with existing works. The performance of the proposed method is not impressive. Please see Table 1. For example, LAPAR/FDIWN/ShuffleMixer perform better in most benchmarks. Moreover, ShuffleMixer and LAPAR use fewer parameters.
3. The compared metrics are incomplete. Since this work focus more on computation efficiency, related metrics such as FLOPS should be computed and compared with existing work, but no supportive metrics are found in the manuscript. I suggest to provide more metrics such as FLOPS to support the efficiency of the proposed model.

[1] Wu, Bichen, et al. "Shift: A zero flop, zero parameter alternative to spatial convolutions." Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition. 2018.
[2] Lin, Ji, Chuang Gan, and Song Han. "Tsm: Temporal shift module for efficient video understanding." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision. 2019.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
[Novelty] As stated above, the novelty is the submission is quite limited. Similar works are [1], [2].
[Clarity] The clarity of this manuscript is satisfactory.
[Reproducibility] The reproducibility is unknown since no code is provided. Also, important compared metrics are missing.


[1] Wu, Bichen, et al. "Shift: A zero flop, zero parameter alternative to spatial convolutions." Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition. 2018.
[2] Lin, Ji, Chuang Gan, and Song Han. "Tsm: Temporal shift module for efficient video understanding." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision. 2019.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Based on the analysis above, I tend to rate rejection for this submission.
Please see "Strength And Weaknesses" for the reasons.

content.title: $1\times1$ Convolution is All You Need for Image Super-Resolution
content.TL;DR: We exploit and demonstrate the effectiveness of the $1\times1$ convolution with spatial-shift  in SR task.
content.abstract:
In resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, lightweight and efficient architectures are crucial for the deployment of single image super-resolution (SISR) deep models. Due to the advantage of achieving a good trade-off between model capacity and efficiency, $3\times3$ convolutions are widely utilized in current convolutional neural networks (CNN). Compared to the normal $3\times3$ convolution, $1\times1$ convolution involves less computation burden but lacks the ability to represent and aggregate spatial information. Accordingly, a common sense in the literature is that  $1\times1$ solely cannot constitute a powerful SR network. In this paper, we revisit $1\times1$ in the lightweight scenario and demonstrate that the fully $1\times1$ convolutional network with strong learning ability can be achieved for SISR, thanks to the manual spatial-shift operation. We investigate the feature aggregation scheme in normal $3\times3$ convolution and analogously extend the $1\times1$ convolution with a parameter-free spatial-shift operation, simplified as the shift-conv layer. 
In the proposed SISR method, we replace all normal $3\times3$ convolutions with shift-conv layers and present the $\mathbf{S}$hift-$\mathbf{C}$onv-based $\mathbf{N}$etwork (SCNet). Extensive experiments demonstrate that SCNets with all $1\times1$ convolutions obtain even better results than SR models with normal $3\times3$ convolutions that have a larger model size.
